title: Desperado & the Mad Rook
subtitle: Doomed pieces sell themselves — sometimes for half a point.
goals: Cash in doomed pieces before they fall
Force stalemate with a rampaging rook

steps.say: A DESPERADO is a piece that knows it's lost — and refuses to die for free. Attacked with no escape? Then grab the biggest thing in reach on the way out. And the ultimate desperado is the MAD ROOK: a rook that checks forever because capturing it would be stalemate. Two versions of the same idea: a doomed piece's value isn't zero — it's whatever it can take with it.

steps.prompt: Mutual knight attacks: yours hangs to the c6 pawn, Black's hangs to your h3 pawn. Most players trade evenly. Squeeze out a profit!
hints: Your knight is doomed no matter what — so its last act should be a capture. With check is even better.
Nxe7+! grabs a pawn and checks; only then do you take on g4. Net result: one extra pawn.

line.say: The desperado — a pawn and a check from a piece that was already dead...
Now the recapture. Black regains the knight with ...Qxe7, but the arithmetic is done: knight for knight, plus e7 in your pocket. Doomed pieces buy groceries on the way to the gallows.

rejections.say: cxd5 — even trade, no profit. Your d5 knight was doomed: before ANY doomed piece dies, ask what it can take with it. Nxe7+ was a free pawn.

You saved the knight... into a pawn-down endgame of retreats — wait, worse: the g4 knight escapes too and you've achieved nothing. When BOTH pieces hang, the side to move should cash a desperado, not run.

steps.wrongSay: The knight can't be saved profitably — so make it eat. Check its reach.
steps.successSay: Desperado arithmetic: doomed piece + in-between capture = profit. Never let a dead piece die hungry.

steps.prompt: Now the immortal swindle. You're BLACK, dead lost — a queen down, king entombed. But look closely: your king has NO legal moves. Weaponize that!
hints: If your rook vanished from the board, you'd have no legal moves at all — and no-moves-plus-no-check is STALEMATE, a draw.
So the rook goes berserk: check forever! Rf1+, Rf2+, Rf3+... capturing it is instant stalemate, and running never escapes the checks.

line.say: The mad rook is loose! Kxf1 would be STALEMATE — your king has no moves and your a6 pawn is blocked. White must run...
...and the rook follows, still untouchable — Kxf2: stalemate again...

Check, forever. Take the rook: stalemate. Run: the checks never end — your rook covers every rank from its file. A full queen down, and the game is a DRAW. The mad rook is the greatest swindle in chess.

rejections.say: Qxf6! and the swindle dies with the rook — a QUIET offer can simply be accepted, because refusing stalemate only matters when refusing is impossible. The rook must arrive with CHECK: checks cannot be declined.
A rook that isn't checking is just a losing rook — White quietly improves the queen and converts the extra material. The magic only works as an endless series of CHECKS: start with Rf1+.

steps.wrongSay: Your immobile king is an asset: it makes every rook capture stalemate. Start checking and never stop.
steps.successSay: The mad rook: perpetual check powered by stalemate. Remember the precondition — your king must have zero moves — and you'll steal half-points from 'lost' positions forever.
